report.summary: Chunk 2 of 7: defines _git_read, resolve_revision, pytest_node_argv, parse_pytest_output, PytestRun, _spawn_pytest, run_node_ids. Enforces worktree safety, revision resolution, pytest invocation, output parsing with per-node attribution and worst-wins ranking.
risks: resolve_revision | low | _git_read uses subprocess.run with timeout; if git hangs, it will raise TimeoutExpired, not return None. | Test with a rev that causes git to hang (e.g. network timeout) and see if exception propagates.
pytest_node_argv | low | Uses sys.executable which may be a virtualenv python; if pytest is not installed there, the call will fail. | Ensure pytest is available in the same environment.

_spawn_pytest | medium | File-based output to a temp dir; if disk is full or permissions fail, OSError is caught and output is set to error message, but the temp dir cleanup may also fail. | Test with disk full or read-only temp dir.
_spawn_pytest | low | ManagedProcess import may fail, then subprocess.run is used; containment string will be 'none' even if job object was intended. | Test without spine.cancel installed.
run_node_ids | medium | Solo re-run for unattributed nodes may itself timeout or fail; no limit on number of solo runs. | Consider adding a max solo retries or timeout per solo run.
parse_pytest_output | medium | FILE_ERROR_RE matches lines like 'ERROR tests/x.py' but the regex is broad; might match unintended lines. | Test with various error messages from pytest.
_same_node | low | Suffix match logic may produce false positives for deeply nested paths. | Test with paths that share suffixes incorrectly.
run_node_ids | medium | Uses _refuse_primary_checkout which may raise a PermissionError or similar; not handled. | Check exception handling in caller.

claims.text: exactly as ``spine.attempt._git`` does for its own choke point.
claims.why: The referenced function is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Deliberately close to ``spine.attempt.pytest_gate_argv``: the same interpreter and the same ``-p no:cacheprovider`` (a gate that dirties the tree it is judging is a trap worth not setting).
claims.why: The referenced function is not in this chunk.

claims.text: It differs in two measured ways, and both are needed for PER-NODE attribution, which ``-q`` cannot give: ``-v`` prints ``<nodeid> PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED (reason)`` per test, which is the only output form that carries the EXACT node id for a skip -- ``-rA``'s short summary prints skips as ``SKIPPED [1] file.py:12: reason``, with no node id at all. ``--tb=no`` the verdict is what is parsed; the traceback is kept in the raw output tail, not in the parse.
claims.why: The function returns argv including '-v' and '--tb=no'.

claims.text: Three spellings have to compare equal, and all three were measured on this box rather than assumed: * pytest prints node ids relative to its rootdir on progress lines, and as an ABSOLUTE path in the ``not found`` line -- so this is a normalised SUFFIX match, not equality; * Windows spells the same file two ways, so it is case-insensitive; * a PARAMETRIZED test is requested as ``file.py::test_x`` and reported as ``file.py::test_x[1]``, once per case. Those report lines belong to the requested node (see :func:`parse_pytest_output`, which reduces several outcomes for one node to the WORST of them, so one red case cannot be averaged away by two green ones).
claims.why: The function normalizes case, checks suffix match, and checks parametrized extension with '['.

claims.text: Worst-wins ranking when one requested node produces several report lines (parametrized cases). A single red case makes the node red -- averaging is exactly the move that hides a fatal blind spot behind an acceptable number.
claims.why: _STATUS_RANK is defined with PASSED lowest and ERROR highest.

claims.text: Per-node status for every requested node id. Never guesses. A node the output says nothing about is ``not_run`` -- not a pass, not a fail. An explicit ``not found`` (``missing``) is final and outranks everything, because the node does not exist; otherwise several report lines for one node reduce to the WORST outcome seen (see ``_STATUS_RANK``); a node with no line of its own inherits ``collect_error`` if its FILE failed to collect.
claims.why: The function initializes all to STATUS_NOT_RUN, then applies missing last, uses _STATUS_RANK for worst-wins, and sets STATUS_COLLECT_ERROR if file error matches.

claims.text: Preferred path is :class:`daedalus.spine.cancel.ManagedProcess`, i.e. a Windows Job Object with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so a hung or forking test tree dies with the run -- the same containment the repo's own pytest gate uses. If that backend is unavailable the run still happens through ``subprocess.run`` and SAYS SO in ``containment``, because a quietly weaker containment that nobody can see is worse than a named one.
claims.why: The code tries ManagedProcess first, falls back to subprocess.run, and sets containment accordingly.

claims.text: Output goes to a file OUTSIDE the worktree: a pipe deadlocks on a chatty run while the parent is polling instead of reading (measured in ``spine.attempt.pytest_gate``, whose shape this follows).
claims.why: The code opens a temp file outside the worktree and writes stdout/stderr to it.

claims.text: Batch first (one interpreter start, ~2.2s on this box, measured), then RE-RUN ALONE every node the batch left unattributed. That fallback is not belt-and-braces, it is required: measured on this box, a single node id pytest cannot collect aborts the WHOLE invocation with exit 4 and nothing else runs -- even with ``--continue-on-collection-errors``. Without the solo re-run, one bad node id would turn every other node in the batch into ``not_run`` and the task into ``could_not_run``.
claims.why: The solo re-run logic is not present in this chunk (chunk ends before that code).

claims.text: ``worktree`` is refused if it is the primary checkout or inside it.
claims.why: The function calls _refuse_primary_checkout which presumably enforces that.

observations.what: resolve_revision uses _git_read which raises subprocess.TimeoutExpired on timeout, not returning None.
pytest_node_argv returns tuple; sys.executable may not have pytest available.
_same_node uses a suffix match that might match unintended nodes if paths share suffixes.
parse_pytest_output uses file_errors list but only checks if path contains '/'; on Windows this might behave differently.
_spawn_pytest catches OSError and sets output to error message; cleanup may also fail silently.
run_node_ids calls _refuse_primary_checkout but does not handle its exceptions.
The solo re-run logic described in run_node_ids docstring is not present in this chunk.
